page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-8 is an x86_64 virtual instance belonging to the Network Optimized server family, configured with a high memory-to-core ratio. The server provides 8 dedicated vCPUs and 124.0 GB of system memory, establishing an allocation of 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include hardware accelerators or graphics processing units.

In terms of peripheral resources, the instance does not feature bundled local storage, requiring network-attached persistent disk options for file system and operating system data. Additionally, it allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses upon provisioning. Storage throughput and network capabilities rely on network interfaces rather than internal NVMe hardware.

The resource profile of the m4n-hypermem-8 emphasizes memory capacity relative to compute threads, offering resource efficiency for workloads that require significant operational memory without necessitating excessive CPU allocations. Due to its 15.5 GB per vCPU density, this instance is suited for in-memory databases, caching engines, real-time analytics aggregation, and memory-intensive ETL tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-8 is an x86_64 architecture instance from the Network Optimized family designed for memory-intensive compute environments. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs and 124.0 GB of system memory, yielding an allocation of 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance is provisioned with zero GPUs and includes no integrated local storage drives, requiring external network-attached storage for host and application data. It also includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By prioritizing memory capacity over raw core count, the m4n-hypermem-8 allows memory-bound services to operate without overpaying for unused processing cores. The instance is structured for workloads such as in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, streaming data pipelines, and analytical processing jobs with heavy RAM requirements.
